title: Regression alerting, diff UI, and triage harness for tok/s and p95
creator: Ava Chen
description: Scope: Build end-to-end support for storing benchmark runs (token/sec, p50/p95/p99, error-rate), a comparison UI that highlights statistically significant performance deltas, and a semi-automated triage workflow so on-call and owners can act quickly on regressions. This ticket covers: (1) storage schema and minimal artifact retention policy, (2) comparison/diff UX prototypes and acceptance criteria, (3) alerting rules and dedupe/auto-bisect hooks, (4) a rerun harness for noisy/unstable signals, and (5) a documented triage playbook integrated with Console rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runs are ingested into the result store with metadata: run_id, commit_sha, model, model_variant, sequence_length_dist, batch_size, hw_type, region, workload_spec_id, start_ts
Time-series metrics (tokens_per_sec, p50, p95, p99, error_rate) are queryable by run_id and aggregated over desired windows within 3s for recent 30d queries
Comparison UI can show side-by-side runs, normalized percent delta, and bootstrap 95% CI for p95 and tokens/sec
Auto-flagging: p95 regressions >= 7% increase or tokens/sec drop >= 10% over stable baseline trigger a perf-alert (configurable per-project)
Triage workflow creates a perf-issue template populated with relevant artifacts (raw traces link, kernel logs, kv-cache hit rate) and assigns an owner when confidence >= 0.8
Rerun harness supports reproducible reruns with identical workload spec and n=30 sampling, writes re-run artifact references to the original run
Console rollout integration blocks canary traffic when an active regression perf-ticket is open and severity is P0
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Chen: Kickoff — aligned with Observability OKR. Primary goal is to reduce blind regressions in runtime. Proposed storage: ClickHouse timeseries + S3 for artifacts.

2026-02-25 Diego Martinez: Spike results — ingest pipeline prototype stores per-req token durations; storing every token trace is too expensive. We'll aggregate per-window (1s buckets) and keep raw traces for failed runs only.
2026-03-01 Product feedback (Maya Patel): UI must surface config diffs (quantization, batch_size) and link to PR that caused model/version change.

2026-03-04 Design review (Eleni Park): Proposed diff UI uses a heatmap timeline and a waterfall list of top 5 delta contributors (seq_len, batch_size, kernel selection). Design asked for clear CTA to trigger rerun.

2026-03-08 Diego Martinez: Decision — statistical test: bootstrap-based CI for p95 and tokens/sec to avoid normality assumptions. Use baseline window = last 7 stable runs. Thresholds set conservatively: 7% p95 increase or 10% tokens/sec drop for auto-alert. We can tune later.
2026-03-10 Eng infra (Sasha Ivanov): Storage trade-off — favor ClickHouse for fast ad-hoc queries; artifacts in S3 with lifecycle 90d and metadata in CH. Cost estimate added to infra board.

2026-03-12 Diego Martinez: Implemented: ingestion lambda + CH schema v1, basic UI mock in Console, and a first alerting pipeline that posts to #perf-regressions Slack. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pulls/2381

implementation_notes: Data model: runs table (run_id PK) + metrics table (run_id, metric_name, bucket_ts, value) + artifacts table (s3_uri, artifact_type, run_id)
Ingestion: push-run endpoint accepts compressed JSONL of per-request summaries; batch commit to CH every 30s
Comparison: UI performs a joined query for two run_ids and computes bootstrap CI client-side if payload small; server-side precomputed summaries for large comparisons
Anomaly engine: periodic job computes deltas vs baseline and scores signal confidence using effect size + sample size; score persisted and used for dedupe
Rerun harness: orchestrator schedules N replays with same seeds, capturing kernel-level telemetry and per-request latencies
Alerting: initial integration to Slack -> optional PagerDuty for severity P0. Tickets create perf triage issue template pre-filled with links
tradeoffs: Full raw-trace retention is expensive; compromise: keep raw traces for failed or flagged runs and aggregate summaries for all runs
Bootstrap CI chosen for robustness but is more CPU-heavy than parametric tests — we precompute for nightly jobs and compute quick CI for ad-hoc comparisons
Thresholds are conservative to avoid alert fatigue; may require tuning in 4-week burn-in
